sources.guyton: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology. 14th edition. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2021.
sources.ase2015: Lang RM, Badano LP, Mor-Avi V, et al. Recommendations for Cardiac Chamber Quantification by Echocardiography in Adults: An Update from the American Society of Echocardiography and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging. J Am Soc Echocardiogr. 2015;28(1):1-39.e14.
sources.aha2022: Heidenreich PA, Bozkurt B, Aguilar D, et al. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines. Circulation. 2022;145(18):e895-e1032.

values.label: End-diastolic volume (LV)
values.where: Chapter 9, The Heart as a Pump: 'End-Diastolic Volume, End-Systolic Volume, and Stroke Volume Output' (about 110 to 120 mL)

values.label: End-systolic volume (LV)
values.where: Chapter 9, 'End-Diastolic Volume, End-Systolic Volume, and Stroke Volume Output' (about 40 to 50 mL)

values.label: Stroke volume
values.where: Chapter 9, 'End-Diastolic Volume, End-Systolic Volume, and Stroke Volume Output' (about 70 mL)
values.note: Single typical value; the source gives no range.

values.label: Ejection fraction (LV)
values.where: Table 2, normal values for 2D echocardiographic LV size and function, LVEF (biplane), men: mean 62, range 52 to 72
values.note: Range shown is for men; the same table gives 54 to 74 % (mean 64) for women. Guyton & Hall, Chapter 9, gives about 60 %.

values.label: Cardiac output (resting)
values.where: Chapter 20, Cardiac Output, Venous Return, and Their Regulation: 'Normal Values for Cardiac Output at Rest and During Activity' (about 5 L/min in the resting adult)
values.note: Single typical value; it varies with body size, sex and age.

values.label: Heart rate
values.where: Chapter 9, 'Cardiac Cycle': duration of the cycle at a normal heart rate of 72 beats/min

values.label: LV systolic pressure (peak)
values.where: Chapter 9, figure 'Events of the cardiac cycle for left ventricular function' (left ventricular pressure curve, peak about 120 mmHg)
values.note: Read from the figure; with a normal aortic valve, peak LV pressure is close to aortic systolic pressure.

values.label: LV end-diastolic pressure
values.where: Chapter 9, 'Volume-Pressure Diagram During the Cardiac Cycle', Phase I (period of filling): diastolic pressure rises to about 5 to 7 mmHg
values.note: In this model LV end-diastolic pressure is approximately equal to the fixed left atrial pressure when filling reaches equilibrium (as at baseline), and falls below it when filling is incomplete (short diastole at high heart rates, or a very compliant ventricle at low preload). This range and the atrial range below only meet at a single shared bound, so the baseline keeps atrial pressure inside its range and the model's LV end-diastolic pressure sits below this one.

values.label: Left atrial pressure (mean) · preload
values.where: Chapter 39, Pulmonary Circulation: 'Left Atrial and Pulmonary Venous Pressures' (averages about 2 mmHg recumbent, from as low as 1 to as high as 5 mmHg)
values.note: In this model atrial pressure is held constant and is the preload slider.

values.label: Aortic (arterial) systolic pressure
values.where: Chapter 15, Vascular Distensibility: 'Arterial Pressure Pulsations' (healthy young adult, about 120 mmHg)

values.label: Aortic (arterial) diastolic pressure
values.where: Chapter 15, 'Arterial Pressure Pulsations' (healthy young adult, about 80 mmHg)

values.label: Pulse pressure
values.where: Chapter 15, 'Arterial Pressure Pulsations' (difference between systolic and diastolic, about 40 mmHg)

values.label: Mean aortic (arterial) pressure
values.where: Chapter 14, Overview of the Circulation: 'Pressures in the Various Portions of the Circulation' (mean aortic pressure averages about 100 mmHg)
values.note: The model's value is the time-average of aortic pressure over the beat.

states.label: Heart failure with reduced EF
states.summary: The left ventricle contracts weakly (a flatter ESPVR), so it ejects a smaller fraction of its volume.
states.context: Only the defining change is listed: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is classified by a reduced LVEF. Other values are not listed because the cited passage does not state them.
states.modelNote: Contractility lowered; preload and heart rate also raised by hand, as an illustration of compensation the model cannot produce itself (it has no kidneys or reflexes).
states.where: Section 2.2, 'Classification of HF by LVEF' (Table 4): HFrEF is HF with reduced LVEF

states.label: Aortic stenosis (pressure-overload afterload)
states.summary: A narrowed aortic valve forces the left ventricle to build a much higher pressure than the aorta to eject.
states.context: Only the change the cited passage states is listed: left ventricular pressure rises during systole. Other values are not listed.
states.modelNote: Not simulated: valve resistance is fixed in this model. Directions only; the model keeps its current settings.
states.where: Chapter 23, Heart Valves and Heart Sounds; Valvular and Congenital Heart Defects: 'Aortic Stenosis and Aortic Regurgitation' (in aortic stenosis the left ventricular pressure rises, sometimes as high as 400 mmHg at the peak of systole)

states.label: Systemic hypertension (raised afterload)
states.summary: Arterial pressure is raised, so the left ventricle must reach a higher pressure before the aortic valve opens.
states.context: Only the defining change is listed: hypertension is defined by a mean arterial pressure above the normal range. Other values are not listed.
states.modelNote: Resistance raised and arterial compliance lowered.
states.where: Chapter 19, Role of the Kidneys in Long-Term Control of Arterial Pressure and in Hypertension: 'Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)' (definition: mean arterial pressure greater than the upper range of normal)

states.label: Hypovolaemia / haemorrhage
states.summary: Lost blood volume lowers the filling pressure of the circulation and venous return, so cardiac output and arterial pressure fall; sympathetic reflexes speed the heart.
states.context: Acute blood loss large enough to lower cardiac output, with reflexes intact and before treatment. Only the changes the cited section states are listed: cardiac output and arterial pressure fall, and heart rate rises through sympathetic reflexes. Other values are not listed.
states.modelNote: Preload lowered and heart rate raised by hand (the model has no baroreflex).
states.where: Chapter 24, Circulatory Shock and Its Treatment: 'Shock Caused by Hypovolemia: Hemorrhagic Shock', 'Relationship of Bleeding Volume to Cardiac Output and Arterial Pressure' and 'Sympathetic Reflex Compensations in Shock' (increased heart rate)

states.label: Positive inotrope
states.summary: Raises the strength of contraction (a steeper ESPVR), so the heart pumps more.
states.context: Only the change the cited passages state is listed: a stronger contraction raises cardiac output. Other values are not listed.
states.modelNote: Contractility raised; atrial pressure stays fixed.
states.where: Chapter 9, 'Control of the Heart by the Sympathetic and Parasympathetic Nerves' (increased force of contraction increases cardiac output) and Chapter 22, 'Treatment of Cardiac Failure' (cardiotonic drugs strengthen the heart)

states.label: Beta-adrenergic blocker
states.summary: Blocks sympathetic beta-receptor effects on the heart, slowing it and weakening its contraction.
states.context: Acute effect at rest in a person with normal resting sympathetic tone. Only the changes the cited passage states for reduced sympathetic stimulation are listed: heart rate and cardiac pumping fall. EF is not given a direction: it can fall acutely as contraction weakens, while long-term treatment of HFrEF improves LVEF (AHA/ACC/HFSA 2022 guideline, Section 7.3.2).
states.modelNote: Heart rate and contractility lowered (the acute case).
states.where: Chapter 9, 'Control of the Heart by the Sympathetic and Parasympathetic Nerves' (decreasing sympathetic stimulation decreases heart rate and strength of contraction, lowering cardiac pumping); Chapter 61, 'Drugs That Block Adrenergic Activity' (beta-receptor blockade)

states.label: Venodilator
states.summary: Dilates veins so more blood pools in them, lowering the filling pressure that drives venous return.
states.context: A drug acting on veins alone, before reflexes respond. Only the change the cited passages state is listed: a lower mean systemic filling pressure lowers venous return and so cardiac output. Other values are not listed.
states.where: Chapter 15, 'Blood Reservoir Function of the Veins'; Chapter 20, 'Venous Return Curves' (a lower mean systemic filling pressure lowers venous return and cardiac output)

states.label: Arterial vasoconstrictor
states.summary: Constricts arterioles and raises systemic vascular resistance, so arterial pressure and afterload rise.
states.context: Arteriolar constriction acting alone, with cardiac output not falling in proportion to the rise in resistance. Because pressure equals flow times resistance, mean arterial pressure rises. Other values are not listed.
states.where: Chapter 17, Local and Humoral Control of Tissue Blood Flow: 'Humoral Control of the Circulation: Vasoconstrictor Agents'; Chapter 14, 'Interrelationships of Pressure, Flow, and Resistance'
